title: Reading long words in small chunks
examples: How do I read a long word?
How do I split a big word?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Big words can look like a giant wall of letters. Here is a trick: break the wall into small chunks. Look at fantastic on the board. It is really just three little bits.

draw.text: Reading long words in small chunks

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Cover the rest with your finger and look at the first chunk: fan. Like a fan that keeps you cool. You can read that! Say it.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Slide your finger along. The next chunk is tas. Say it. Each chunk is short and easy. Can you read it on its own?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Last chunk: tic, like the tick of a clock. Now push the chunks together: fan, tas, tic. Fantastic! That is exactly what you are. Can you feel how much easier one chunk at a time is?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: One small chunk at a time.

explain.say: Try this one: remember. Three chunks: re, mem, ber. Tip: each chunk usually has one vowel sound. Super chunking! Challenge: try the word important. How many chunks can you find?

faq.a: Chunking means cutting a long word into small parts, then reading one part at a time. Fan, tas and tic make fantastic.

faq.q: How do I know where to split a word?
faq.a: Look for the vowels. Each chunk usually has one vowel sound. Clapping the word helps you hear the chunks too.
asks: Where do I break a long word?

faq.q: What if I split the word in the wrong place?
faq.a: That is okay! Try a different split and listen. Does it sound like a word you know? A teacher or grown-up can help you find the chunks.

faq.q: Can I use my finger or a card to help?
faq.a: Yes! Cover the word and slide your finger or a card along, showing one chunk at a time. It helps your eyes stay on just one bit.
asks: How do I cover the word?

faq.q: Do chunks work for really long words?
faq.a: Yes. Even hippopotamus is just five chunks: hip, po, pot, a, mus. Every big word is made of small bits.

facts: Fantastic has three syllables: fan, tas and tic.

quiz.say: How many chunks are in the word remember?

wrong.0: Clap it: re, mem, ber. That is one more than two.
wrong.2: Remember has three beats, not four.
